title: Roman Catechism correction: one may also ask Saints themselves to pity and help by grace and deprecation
source_text: LVII. Et similiter Catechesis Romana, postquam dixit ad Deum dici Miserere nobis, ad Sanctum, Ora pro nobis, per correctionem quandam, ut mentem suam explicet, subjungit, Quanquam etiam licet alia quadam ratione petere a Sanctis ipsis ut nostri misereantur: sunt enim maxime misericordes: itaque possumus precari eos, ut conditionis nostrae miseria permoti, sua nos apud Deum gratia, & deprecatione juvent.
pass_a_gloss: And likewise the Roman Catechesis, after it has said that to God is said Have mercy on us, to a Saint, Pray for us, by a certain correction, that it may explain its mind, subjoins: Although it is also lawful in another certain way to ask of the Saints themselves that they pity us: for they are most merciful: and so we can pray them that, moved by the misery of our condition, they help us before God by their grace and deprecation.
pass_b_english: After ‘Ora pro nobis,’ the Catechism corrects: you may also ask Saints themselves to pity you.
Moved by our misery, they help before God by their grace and prayer.

choices.term: Quanquam etiam licet alia quadam ratione
choices.english: Although it is also lawful in another way
choices.why: Catechism’s softener after the strict formula contrast.
